# Thin curve native controls

Original XML geometry generated by `tools/thin_curve_native_fixture.py` using
existing original fixture helpers, lxml and the Python standard library. No
template artwork, font program or third-party document engine is included.
Generate into a fresh directory; `source.docx` and `cases.json` are deterministic.

Sixteen Letter pages each contain a grouped 100x60pt rectangle and ellipse,
without fills, using C0C0C0 round pens. Four physical widths (1588, 3175, 4327,
6350 EMU) cross four page-position phases (0, .25, .5, .75pt). Body margins are
72pt. The source contains no authored text; its drawing paragraph requests the
ordinary installed Arial font. The reference application emitted font metadata and one clipped
Unicode space per metafile. These captures must not be described as having no
text drawing records. There are no embedded font programs.

The reference application emitted the compressed metafiles on 2026-10-10. `native.json`
records source/metafile hashes, unchanged source, matching Saved states and
unchanged view. An earlier capture failed the Saved-state guard and is excluded.
All 32 EMF+ pen objects preserve the authored EMU width with World units under
the recorded world-to-device transform. Group-level reference Line API values are
not used as individual-child measurements.

The browser regression checks editable import, 16 print sheets, exact no-edit
export/undo, controlled text insertion, unrelated package-part preservation and
editable reopen. Schema checks passed for source and edited exports (8 views).
This proves neither an exact native pixel match nor correct physical print pens.

The later physical-print regression covers anchored and inline frame variants,
measures actual Canvas pen widths against the retained native PDF's physical
rule, and checks that screen pixels survive printing unchanged. The inline
variant retains this original geometry and changes only the containing frame.
It is schema-checked separately. Complete native raster agreement remains open.
